answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds identity registration to a verifiable burn of cryptographic collateral. In the Sparrow protocol, each newly spawned node must submit a proof-of-burn commitment alongside a jade validation key, permanently destroying native tokens. Total entry costs scale via superlinear cost scaling C(k) = k^{1.5}, forcing an attacker attempting to deploy a pearl cluster of forged identities to incur exponentially ruinous capital loss.
